items.title: Section: All Ten Roots Now Traced — Which Poison Actually Completes Each Path

items.zh: 若不如理於法思惟、籌量、觀察，由此方便所引尋伺，發起邪見，名癡所生邪見業道。復次，殺生業道三為方便，由瞋究竟。如殺業道，麁語、瞋恚業道亦爾。不與取業道三為方便，由貪究竟。如不與取，邪行、貪欲業道亦爾。除其邪見，所餘業道三為方便，由三究竟。邪見業道三為方便，由癡究竟。
items.en: Unreasoned thinking, faulty reflection, and mistaken examination of the dharmas, giving rise through this means to discursive thought that generates wrong view, is wrong view generated by delusion. Moreover, the karma-path of killing takes all three as its means, but is completed by hatred. As with the karma-path of killing, so too harsh speech and malice. The karma-path of taking what is not given takes all three as its means, but is completed by greed. As with taking what is not given, so too sexual misconduct and covetousness. Apart from wrong view, the remaining karma-paths take all three as their means, and are completed by all three. The karma-path of wrong view takes all three as its means, but is completed by delusion.

items.title: Section: Four Groundings for Ten Karma-Paths

items.zh: 復次，殺生、邪行、妄語、離間、麁語、瞋恚，此六業道有情處起。不與而取、貪欲業道，資財處起。綺語業道，名身處起。邪見業道，諸行處起。復次，由三因緣，不善業道成極圓滿惡不善性。
items.en: Moreover, killing, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, and malice, these six karma-paths arise with respect to sentient beings. Taking what is not given and covetousness arise with respect to wealth. The karma-path of idle chatter arises with respect to the name-body. The karma-path of wrong view arises with respect to conditioned formations. Moreover, through three causes and conditions, an unwholesome karma-path becomes fully complete in its own unwholesome, evil nature.

items.title: Section: A Victim's Own Suffering Measures the Crime

items.zh: 何等為三？一、自性過故；二、因緣過故；三、塗染過故。此中殺生所引思，乃至邪見所引彼相應思，如是一切染污性故、不善性故，由自性過說名為惡。若以猛利貪欲、瞋恚、愚癡纏所發起，即此亦名由因緣過，成重惡性、成上不善，能引增上不可愛果。若到究竟，即此亦名由塗染過，成極重惡，成上不善，能引增上不可愛果。何以故？若有用染污心，能引發他不可愛樂欣悅之苦，彼隨苦心威勢力故，能引發苦補特伽羅思，便觸得廣大之罪，是故名為塗染過失。彼雖不發如是相心：諸能引發我之苦者，當觸大罪。然彼法爾觸於大罪。譬如礠石雖不作意：諸所有鐵來附於我。然彼法爾所有近鐵，不由功用來附礠石。此中道理，當知亦爾。日珠等喻，亦如是知。
items.en: What are the three? First, the intrinsic-nature fault. Second, the causal-condition fault. Third, the contamination fault. Here, the volition drawn forth by killing, down through the volition drawn forth by wrong view, being entirely defiled and unwholesome in nature, is called evil through this intrinsic-nature fault. If driven by forceful greed, hatred, or delusion, this is likewise called, through the causal-condition fault, becoming a grave, superior unwholesome nature capable of drawing forth an undesirable result. If reaching completion, this is likewise called, through the contamination fault, becoming an extremely grave, superior unwholesome nature capable of drawing forth an undesirable result. If a defiled mind draws forth in another an unwanted, unwelcome suffering, then, through the force of that being's suffering mind, the volition of the person who drew forth that suffering incurs a vast offence; this is called the contamination fault. Though the victim generates no such thought as, may whoever causes me this suffering incur a great offence, a great offence is naturally incurred regardless. Just as a lodestone, without willing that iron come cling to it, still has iron naturally cling nearby without any exertion — this principle should be understood the same way. The sun-crystal offers the same illustration.

items.title: Section: Māra's Corruption, and the Fire Already Latent in Every Deed

items.zh: 又於思上無別有法，彼威力生來相依附，說名塗染。當知唯是此思轉變，由彼威力之所發起。如四大種業威勢力所生種種堅性、濕性、煖性、動性，非大種外別有如是種種諸性，然即大種業威勢緣，如是轉變。如業威勢緣力轉變，神足加行緣力轉變，當知亦爾。又如魔王，惑媚無量娑梨藥迦諸婆羅門長者等心，令於世尊變異暴惡。非於彼心更增別法，說名惑媚。唯除魔王加行威勢生彼諸心，令其轉變成極暴惡。此中道理，當知亦爾。
items.en: Also, it is not that, over and above volition, some separate dharma arises from the power of that defiled mind and comes to cling to it, and is called contamination. It should be known that this is simply volition's own transformation, arisen through that very power. Just as the great elements' own force gives rise to solidity, wetness, warmth, and motion, these qualities not existing apart from the elements themselves, but being the elements' own force so transformed — as with the transformation wrought by karma's own force, so too the transformation wrought by the force of psychic accomplishment. Just as Māra corrupted the hearts of countless brahmin elders and householders, turning them hostile towards the Blessed One, not by adding any separate dharma to their minds, this being called corruption, but purely through Māra's own scheming power giving rise to those very minds, turning them into extreme hostility — this same principle should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: Stealing Then Killing — One Act or Two?

items.zh: 復次，如先所說作及增長業，若先所說由五因緣成極重業，名定受業。與此相違，名不定受業。復有四業。一、異熟定，二、時分定，三、二俱定，四、二俱不定。諸阿羅漢所有不善決定受業，或於前生所作，或於此生先異生位所作，由少輕苦之所逼惱，便名果報已熟。若已轉依，果報種子皆永斷故，一切不受。所以者何？由佛世尊依未解脫相續，建立定受業故。問：若於一時亦牽亦搦，盜取眾生，即斷其命。當言一業，為二業耶？答：當言二業。以速轉故，於此二業，由增上慢，謂之為一。
items.en: Moreover, as already explained regarding karma committed and increased, if the five causes and conditions already explained are complete, an extremely grave karma results, called certain karma. Opposite to this is called uncertain karma. There are also four kinds of karma: certain in ripening result, certain in timing, certain in both, or uncertain in both. Whatever certain, definitely-to-be-experienced unwholesome karma an arhat carries, whether committed in a past life or in this life during an earlier unawakened state, is experienced through only a slight, light discomfort, and this is called the ripened result. Once the transformed basis is attained, the seeds of that result are permanently severed, and none of it is experienced at all. Question: if, in one continuous motion, one both takes and kills a creature, stealing it and then ending its life, should this be called one karma or two? Answer: it should be called two. Because of the rapid succession, a mistaken notion arising from confusion about number takes these two karmas for one.

items.zh: 若謂我當牽彼，是第一思；即於盜時，復謂我當搦殺，是第二思。若時牽彼，爾時不搦；若時搦彼，爾時不牽；速疾轉故，生增上慢，謂是一時。是故此中，當言二業。

blocks.text: Which poison "completes" each deed, what each rests on, and when karma is certain to ripen.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "completion" means the most frequent and gravest case, enough to bring ripening. Though all three poisons may begin a killing, hatred completes it; greed completes theft.
Master Cháng Bǎi: six usually rest on beings; theft and covetousness on wealth; idle chatter on names; wrong view on all conditioned things.
Master Cháng Bǎi: harming a being is itself a fault, and a great offence follows naturally. Though the harmer does not intend to incur an offence, the defiled nature of karma brings it.
Master Cháng Bǎi: apart from the evil volition there is no further thing called "killing"; Māra adds no other thing to the mind.

Master Cháng Bǎi: with all conditions complete, karma is very heavy and certain to be experienced; if countered by practice, absorption, or the noble path, its time of ripening becomes uncertain. Arhats have severed affliction's seeds forever, so nothing moistens past karma and no ripening comes. Taking a fowl and then killing it is two acts: the mind moves so fast that one mistakes two for one. (Untranslated, 0635c14: the treatise's reasoning: "I will lead it off" and "I will kill it" are two volitions; they do not occur at once.)
"If countered by practice, the time of ripening becomes uncertain." Karma is not fate; practice changes how and whether it ripens.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 究竟 in "completed by hatred"?
options: the highest attainment, or the bare finishing of the act
the moment of death
the end of karmic result
most frequent, gravest, reaching the degree that brings ripening
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 究竟 means what is most frequent and gravest, reaching the degree of bringing ripening. Though all three poisons may begin killing, hatred completes it. The English "completed by hatred" is correct, if brief.

quiz.q: Which paths are completed by hatred, and which by greed?
options: theft, misconduct, covetousness by hatred; killing and the rest by greed, theft being angry and killing for gain
all ten by delusion
the speech paths by hatred
killing, harsh speech, malice; theft, misconduct, covetousness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: greed is the chief affliction in theft, the most common and gravest case. The pattern is six paths divided by hatred and greed, three speech paths by all three, and wrong view by delusion. The English states it plainly.

quiz.q: Which paths are completed by all three, and what of wrong view?
options: false, divisive, idle speech, as any poison may speak; wrong view by delusion
only harsh speech; wrong view by greed for one's views
the bodily paths; wrong view by hatred
the mental paths; wrong view by all three
quiz.why: After the six and wrong view, three speech paths remain: false, divisive, and idle. Master Cháng Bǎi names divisive and false speech, and his count in that line omits idle chatter, so the list here follows the treatise. Wrong view, though begun by all three, is completed by delusion.

quiz.q: What are the four bases of the ten paths?
options: beings six; wealth two; name-body one; formations one
three each by body, speech, and mind, with wrong view alone
all ten rest on beings
all ten rest on formations
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these six usually rest on beings; theft and covetousness on wealth. Idle chatter rests on names, wrong view on all conditioned things. The English "name-body" is literal for 名身. The grouping is by object, not by the three doors.

quiz.q: Why does idle chatter rest on the name-body and wrong view on formations?
options: idle chatter on the body speaking; wrong view on nirvāṇa, unconditioned
both on wealth
both on beings
words in the mind yield pointless speech; wrong view rests on all conditioned things
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind holds many words and sentiments, and from these, pointless speech arises; wrong view rests on all conditioned things such as the aggregates and the world. The English "conditioned formations" is accurate; "name-body" needs a note.

quiz.q: Through which three is an unwholesome path fully complete in evil?
options: seen, heard, and suspected, as in the Vinaya, nature and condition being the lecturer's additions
intrinsic-nature, causal-condition, and contamination fault
greed, hatred, delusion
body, speech, mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: three conditions make an unwholesome path fully evil, certainly leading to ripening in hell; the volition-moving wish is defiled and unwholesome. The English "contamination fault" renders 塗染 fairly well.

quiz.q: How do the causal-condition and contamination faults differ?
options: past karma and present defamation, 塗染 meaning stained reputation, unrelated to victims or completion
they are the same
forceful affliction joined with volition is the former; completion and the victim's pain the latter
the first higher, the second desire-realm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: forceful affliction joined with volition is the causal fault; the ten evils reaching completion is the contamination fault, and the offence is as great as the victim's suffering. The English drops 增上 before "undesirable result" in both.

quiz.q: The English has "a vast offence is incurred." What is left out?
options: it omits the sufferer-causing person's volition: the harmer's volition is what incurs it
nothing: the victim incurs it, 苦補特伽羅 being the sufferer, as the lecture says
it omits 廣大
it omits 苦
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: harming a being is itself a fault, and a great offence follows naturally. So the one incurring it is the harmer, whose volition caused the suffering. The English passive leaves that unstated, though this is the key of the contamination fault.

quiz.q: What does the lodestone simile show?
options: without the victim's wish, the harmer naturally incurs great offence
the harmer needs intent, as a magnet must will it
iron heats the magnet
the Buddha's attraction
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though the harmer does not intend to incur an offence, the defiled, unwholesome nature of karma is such, and so the deed brings it. The simile says there need be no wish on anyone's part: the law works by nature, as iron goes to a lodestone.

quiz.q: The English has "its own inherent power arises and naturally clings to it." What is wrong with the negation's scope?
options: no problem: no other dharma, but a power clings to volition, called contamination, no conflict arising
"volition" should be "form"
the treatise denies a separate dharma arising to cling; the English affirms power clinging, against the next line
"called" should be "denied"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the similes show that apart from the evil volition there is no further thing called killing. The treatise's own parallel, "not adding a separate dharma to their minds," confirms the negation covers the whole clause. Split in two, the English asserts what the next sentence denies.

quiz.q: What is the point of the Māra simile?
options: Māra puts seeds in their minds, an outer thing transferable from others
Māra outdoes the Buddha
Māra adds no separate dharma, only changing the mind; karma is likewise volition transformed
the brahmins were already evil
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: Māra does not add another dharma to their minds. The ten evils rest on intrinsic fault, gain causal fault with strong poisons, and on completion become great evil, habituating seeds of evil volition. So contamination is not an added substance.

quiz.q: The English has "the great elements' own force gives rise to." What is left out?
options: nothing: 業 means function here, the elements having their own, the next line's "karma" being the error
it omits 業: karma's force conditions the elements, and it does not join "karma's own force" next
it omits 四
it omits 性
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: as karma's force is a condition for change, so with psychic power. The treatise's own "as with karma's force" shows the first clause too is about karma. Dropping 業 from it breaks the parallel with the psychic-power clause.

quiz.q: How do certain and uncertain karma differ?
options: wholesome karma is certain and evil uncertain, repentance removing it
past certain; future uncertain
committed, increased, and very grave through the five is certain; the opposite uncertain
bodily certain; verbal uncertain
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with these conditions complete it is very heavy karma, certain to be experienced; without them it is uncertain. So the whole earlier analysis of gravity pays off here. The English "certain karma" is fine.

quiz.q: What are the four kinds of karma, and what makes it uncertain?
options: bodily, verbal, mental, neutral, unrelated to ripening or timing
certain in result, in time, both, neither; antidotes making timing uncertain
black, white, mixed, neither
of the three realms and unbound
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: after karma is made, if it has been countered by the force of practice, absorption, or the noble path, the time of ripening is uncertain. So practice affects when and whether a result comes. The English list is accurate.

quiz.q: What of an arhat's certain unwholesome karma, and after the transformed basis?
options: arhats still go to hell, karma being fixed, only for less time
slight pain counts as ripened; seeds severed, nothing moistens it, no ripening at all
the Buddha bears it for them
it is transferred to beings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: since arhats have severed affliction seeds forever, nothing moistens or triggers past karmic seeds, and so no ripening is experienced. The treatise adds that a slight pain counts as ripening. The source's rationale sentence on certainty is missing from the English.

quiz.q: The English has "an overreaching conceit" here. Why is that poor in this place?
options: fine: it is pride in doing two things at once, the same as §6, as the lecture says
it should be "anger"
it should be "faith"
here it is a numerical confusion, not §6's claim of virtue; one word suggests pride
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 增上慢 here belongs to confusion about objects; through confusing the number, one mistakes two karmas for one. So it is a cognitive error about count, unrelated to pride. The English should say "mistaken notion" or add a note.

quiz.q: Why is seizing and killing a creature at once two karmas?
options: one motion is one karma, 二業 being a manner of speaking, only separate acts counting
two creatures
taking is theft and throttling is killing; a quick mind thinks them one
two doers
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind moves quickly; one first takes another's fowl, and then kills it. So theft and killing are two karmas though they seem one. The treatise's argument that two distinct volitions occur is absent from the English.
